summary: Arq is a niche activated carbon producer reliant on coal-fired power plants for demand and coal waste for feedstock. Its deep drawdown reflects cyclical and regulatory risk; the thesis bets on sustained MATS enforcement and stable feedstock costs. Supply chain is concentrated in US coal regions with few substitutes.

inputs.whyNeeded: primary raw material for activated carbon production
inputs.concentration: high (limited to coal mining regions, few suppliers)
inputs.fragility: high (dependent on coal mine output and waste availability)

chokepoints.why: only manufacturing site; any outage halts output
few coal mines produce suitable waste; contract renewal risk

customers.why: MATS rule mandates mercury capture; primary demand driver
activated carbon for filtration; secondary market

supplyChain.geographic: US-centric (Appalachia for feedstock, Midwest/Southeast for power plant customers); limited international exposure
substitutes: coconut-shell-based activated carbon (imported, lower cost but less effective for mercury)
dry sorbent injection (alternative mercury control technology)

bearCase: EPA MATS rule weakened or repealed, collapsing demand from coal plants.
Coal plant retirements accelerate, shrinking customer base faster than expected.
Feedstock cost spikes (coal waste scarcity or transport disruption) squeeze margins.
Corbin plant operational failure (fire, regulatory shutdown) stops all revenue.

loadBearing.assumption: US coal-fired generation stays above 150 GW for 1-2 years
loadBearing.breaksIf: coal plant retirements accelerate due to cheap gas or renewables; generation drops below 150 GW

loadBearing.assumption: EPA MATS rule remains in force or strengthened
loadBearing.breaksIf: EPA weakens enforcement or court vacates rule; power plants stop buying mercury-control carbon

loadBearing.assumption: Arq secures coal-waste feedstock at stable/declining cost
loadBearing.breaksIf: coal mine closures reduce waste supply; transportation costs rise; contract renegotiation fails

loadBearing.assumption: No catastrophic operational failure at Corbin plant
loadBearing.breaksIf: fire, explosion, or regulatory shutdown at single facility; no backup capacity

prediction.statement: Q2 2026 earnings (Aug 2026) will show revenue decline >10% YoY due to coal plant retirements and MATS uncertainty.
prediction.resolutionCriterion: Actual Q2 2026 revenue reported vs prior year; decline >10% confirms bearish supply-chain pressure.

gaps: No detailed breakdown of customer contracts or revenue concentration.
No feedstock cost trend data or supplier names.
No capacity utilization or maintenance schedule for Corbin plant.
verifyThese: Check EPA MATS rule status and any pending legal challenges.
Verify coal plant retirements announced in Arq's service region.
Confirm Arq's feedstock supply agreements and renewal dates.
Check Corbin plant insurance and operational history.
diminishingReturns: Stopped at coal waste and power plant demand; deeper hops (e.g., coal mine geology, mercury sorbent chemistry) do not change investment picture because the core risk is regulatory and plant retirements, not input minutiae.
